column7: Original discrete analog design with two parallel gain circuits; High and Low controls combine gain and bias, Filter changes tonal emphasis with circuit state, Input controls headroom/saturation, Master controls output. 2023 coverage documents the design and a Finnish production origin.
column10: Highly unusual High/Low bias-gain interaction and five-control surface make this a strong specimen identifier; preserve fuzz capability without recategorizing it as a generic fuzz.

column7: Compact dual-drive combining independently controlled Test Tube and Lab Rat sections with universal Level and Blend controls. Contemporary 2023 coverage describes the combined architecture and identifies maker Mark Turley; exact first-production date remains unresolved.
column10: Treat the two-channel architecture and shared Level/Blend interface as core product identity. Do not confuse 2023 coverage with a guaranteed 2023 introduction date.

column7: Brand-new Tulsa, Oklahoma builder's debut pedal, introduced in March 2023. Fully analog with Gain, Output, Bass and Treble controls plus a three-way clipping toggle: symmetrical, asymmetrical and cross-asymmetrical.
column10: The 3-way clipping switch and Bass/Treble layout are strong external identifiers. Preserve its debut-product status separately from later builder releases.

column7: 2023 coverage documents a high-range overdrive using an OP275 front end, two clipping modes including Soviet germanium diode option, Fat and LP/HP voicing switches, integrated boost, and internal voltage doubling to 18V for the op-amp stage.
column10: Control density and the named OP275/Ge clipping configuration are useful identification evidence. Keep Albert separate from Tephra even though both are hybridized classic-style gain designs from the same builder.

column7: Ohmless describes AKC-4 as its second attempt after the 2013 Lorena. 2023 coverage documents four footswitch/MIDI-selectable clipping options, pre/post boost placement and broad low-to-mid distortion range. Builder-generation boundary needs primary dating enrichment.
column10: Preserve AKC-4 as a distinct product from Lorena. The four selectable clipping modes and MIDI/footswitch control are high-value identification clues.

column6: Dual overdrive / Blues Breaker + Klon lineage
column7: Two independent overdrives in one enclosure. Left side uses breaker-style roots with Drive, Tone and Level plus Saturation/transparency switching; right side is a hard-clipping K-style drive with Low, High, Gain and Level. Order toggle reverses the signal path; soft-touch momentary footswitches and 9V operation documented.
column10: 2023 introduction is supported by contemporary September coverage. The two distinct sides, order toggle, separate footswitches and asymmetric control sets make the product highly identifiable.
